Report introduction: This report describes a programme for comfortable upper-body movement.
General safety: Use the report-level monitoring and referral guidance before selecting an exercise.

Name: Chin tuck
Purpose: Practise gentle head and neck alignment.
Exercise type: Motor-control and endurance
Targeted musclegroups: Neck stabilisers; upper back
Targeted specific muscles: musculus longus colli; musculus trapezius
Equipment and environment: A wall and a clear floor space
Starting position and set-up: Stand comfortably with the back supported.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Use a small controlled range.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Reduce the range.
Progression: Add a brief controlled hold.
Common errors and corrections: Lifting the chin—Keep the gaze level.
Evidence category: Motor-control exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Wall angel
Purpose: Practise shoulder movement with a comfortable trunk position.
Exercise type: Mobility and motor-control
Targeted musclegroups: Shoulder girdle; upper back
Targeted specific muscles: musculus serratus anterior; musculus trapezius
Equipment and environment: A clear wall
Starting position and set-up: Stand with the back near a wall.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Keep the movement smooth and pain free.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Stand farther from the wall.
Progression: Increase the controlled range.
Common errors and corrections: Arching the back—Use a smaller range.
Evidence category: Mobility exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Scapular retraction
Purpose: Practise controlled shoulder-blade movement.
Exercise type: Resistance strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Shoulder girdle; upper back
Targeted specific muscles: musculus rhomboideus; musculus trapezius
Equipment and environment: A chair and clear space
Starting position and set-up: Sit or stand tall with relaxed shoulders.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Draw the shoulder blades gently together.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Use less range.
Progression: Add light resistance.
Common errors and corrections: Shrugging the shoulders—Keep them relaxed.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Thoracic extension over chair
Purpose: Practise comfortable thoracic extension.
Exercise type: Thoracic mobility
Targeted musclegroups: Thoracic spinal extensors; trunk stabilisers
Targeted specific muscles: musculus erector spinae; musculus multifidus
Equipment and environment: A sturdy chair
Starting position and set-up: Sit with the chair back supporting the upper back.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Extend only as far as comfortable.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild movement without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Use a smaller range.
Progression: Pause briefly at the end of the range.
Common errors and corrections: Extending the neck—Keep the head supported.
Evidence category: Mobility exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Cat-camel
Purpose: Explore comfortable spinal movement.
Exercise type: Mobility and motor-control
Targeted musclegroups: Trunk; shoulder girdle
Targeted specific muscles: musculus erector spinae; musculus rectus abdominis
Equipment and environment: A mat or carpet
Starting position and set-up: Start on hands and knees.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Use a gentle alternating range.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild movement without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Reduce the range.
Progression: Make each phase slower.
Common errors and corrections: Rushing the movement—Move more slowly.
Evidence category: Mobility exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Open book rotation
Purpose: Practise comfortable thoracic rotation.
Exercise type: Thoracic mobility
Targeted musclegroups: Thoracic spine; shoulder girdle
Targeted specific muscles: musculus obliquus externus abdominis; musculus erector spinae
Equipment and environment: A mat and clear floor space
Starting position and set-up: Lie on one side with knees comfortably bent.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Rotate the upper trunk without forcing the knees apart.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions per side with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild movement without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Use a smaller range.
Progression: Pause briefly at the open position.
Common errors and corrections: Rolling the knees—Keep the legs supported.
Evidence category: Mobility exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Doorway pectoral stretch
Purpose: Practise a comfortable chest stretch.
Exercise type: Flexibility and mobility
Targeted musclegroups: Chest; shoulder girdle
Targeted specific muscles: musculus pectoralis major; musculus pectoralis minor
Equipment and environment: A clear doorway
Starting position and set-up: Stand in a doorway with one forearm supported.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly into the comfortable stretch.
Range and direction: Turn away only until a mild stretch is felt.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Hold for twenty seconds with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild stretch without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Step less far forward.
Progression: Increase the hold gradually.
Common errors and corrections: Forcing the stretch—Use less range.
Evidence category: Flexibility exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Prone cobra
Purpose: Practise posterior shoulder and trunk endurance.
Exercise type: Postural strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Upper back; shoulder girdle
Targeted specific muscles: musculus trapezius; musculus erector spinae
Equipment and environment: A mat and clear floor space
Starting position and set-up: Lie face down with the forehead supported.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Lift only as far as control is maintained.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Keep the arms by the sides.
Progression: Hold the lifted position briefly.
Common errors and corrections: Shrugging the shoulders—Lengthen the neck.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Wall slide
Purpose: Practise controlled overhead shoulder movement.
Exercise type: Mobility and motor-control
Targeted musclegroups: Shoulder girdle; upper back
Targeted specific muscles: musculus serratus anterior; musculus trapezius
Equipment and environment: A clear wall
Starting position and set-up: Stand with the back near a wall.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Slide the arms upward without forcing contact.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Stand farther from the wall.
Progression: Increase the controlled range.
Common errors and corrections: Flaring the ribs—Use a smaller range.
Evidence category: Mobility exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Band pull-apart
Purpose: Build controlled upper-back endurance.
Exercise type: Resistance strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Upper back; shoulder girdle
Targeted specific muscles: musculus trapezius; musculus deltoideus
Equipment and environment: A light resistance band
Starting position and set-up: Hold the band at chest height with relaxed shoulders.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Separate the hands without arching the back.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Eight repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Use a lighter band.
Progression: Use a slightly stronger band.
Common errors and corrections: Bending the elbows—Keep the arms long.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Resistance-band row
Purpose: Build controlled pulling strength.
Exercise type: Resistance strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Upper back; arms
Targeted specific muscles: musculus latissimus dorsi; musculus biceps brachii
Equipment and environment: A securely anchored resistance band
Starting position and set-up: Sit or stand facing the anchor with the band held securely.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Draw the elbows back without shrugging.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Eight repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Use a lighter band.
Progression: Increase band resistance.
Common errors and corrections: Leaning backward—Keep the trunk steady.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Y raise
Purpose: Build controlled shoulder-girdle endurance.
Exercise type: Postural strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Shoulder girdle; upper back
Targeted specific muscles: musculus trapezius; musculus deltoideus
Equipment and environment: A mat or clear standing space
Starting position and set-up: Stand or lie face down with the arms relaxed.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Raise the arms in a comfortable Y shape.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Keep the arms lower.
Progression: Add light resistance.
Common errors and corrections: Shrugging the shoulders—Keep the neck long.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Serratus wall slide
Purpose: Practise upward shoulder-blade rotation.
Exercise type: Motor-control and strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Shoulder girdle; chest
Targeted specific muscles: musculus serratus anterior; musculus pectoralis minor
Equipment and environment: A clear wall
Starting position and set-up: Stand facing the wall with the forearms supported.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Slide the forearms upward without forcing the shoulders.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Slide through a smaller range.
Progression: Add a light band around the wrists.
Common errors and corrections: Losing contact suddenly—Move more slowly.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Reverse fly
Purpose: Build controlled posterior shoulder strength.
Exercise type: Resistance strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Upper back; posterior shoulder
Targeted specific muscles: musculus deltoideus; musculus trapezius
Equipment and environment: Light weights and clear space
Starting position and set-up: Hinge comfortably with the arms hanging below the shoulders.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Open the arms without twisting the trunk.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Eight repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Use no weights.
Progression: Add small amounts of load.
Common errors and corrections: Swinging the arms—Use lighter weights.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Bird-dog
Purpose: Practise trunk control while the limbs move.
Exercise type: Motor-control and endurance
Targeted musclegroups: Trunk stabilisers; hip extensors
Targeted specific muscles: musculus transversus abdominis; musculus gluteus maximus
Equipment and environment: A mat or carpet
Starting position and set-up: Start on hands and knees with a comfortable spine.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Reach long rather than high.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions per side with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Move one limb at a time.
Progression: Increase the hold gradually.
Common errors and corrections: Rotating the pelvis—Shorten the reach.
Evidence category: Motor-control exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Glute bridge
Purpose: Build hip extension strength with a steady trunk.
Exercise type: Resistance strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Hip extensors; trunk
Targeted specific muscles: musculus gluteus maximus; musculus biceps femoris
Equipment and environment: A mat or carpet
Starting position and set-up: Lie on the back with knees bent and feet supported.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Lift the pelvis without forcing the lower back.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Eight repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Lift through a smaller range.
Progression: Pause at the top.
Common errors and corrections: Arching the back—Lift less high.
Evidence category: Strength exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Plank
Purpose: Build controlled trunk endurance.
Exercise type: Strengthening and endurance
Targeted musclegroups: Trunk; shoulder girdle
Targeted specific muscles: musculus transversus abdominis; musculus rectus abdominis
Equipment and environment: A mat and clear floor space
Starting position and set-up: Support the body on forearms and knees.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly into the supported position.
Range and direction: Keep the trunk steady without sagging.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Hold for ten seconds with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Keep the knees supported.
Progression: Extend the hold gradually.
Common errors and corrections: Holding the breath—Breathe continuously.
Evidence category: Trunk endurance exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Dead bug
Purpose: Practise trunk control during limb movement.
Exercise type: Motor-control and endurance
Targeted musclegroups: Trunk; hip flexors
Targeted specific muscles: musculus transversus abdominis; musculus iliopsoas
Equipment and environment: A mat or carpet
Starting position and set-up: Lie on the back with hips and knees comfortably bent.
Step-by-step movement: Move slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Lower one limb without losing a comfortable trunk position.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions per side with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Move one limb at a time.
Progression: Increase the range gradually.
Common errors and corrections: Arching the back—Shorten the lever.
Evidence category: Motor-control exercise
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Sit-to-stand
Purpose: Practise a functional lower-body movement.
Exercise type: Functional resistance strengthening
Targeted musclegroups: Thighs; hips
Targeted specific muscles: musculus quadriceps femoris; musculus gluteus maximus
Equipment and environment: A sturdy chair and clear space
Starting position and set-up: Sit near the front of a sturdy chair with feet supported.
Step-by-step movement: Stand and sit slowly with control.
Range and direction: Keep the knees tracking comfortably over the feet.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Five repetitions with thirty seconds rest.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Use a higher seat.
Progression: Use a lower seat or light load.
Common errors and corrections: Knees collapsing inward—Push evenly through the feet.
Evidence category: Functional strengthening
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes

Name: Walking posture drill
Purpose: Practise comfortable upright walking.
Exercise type: Aerobic and postural activity
Targeted musclegroups: Lower limbs; trunk
Targeted specific muscles: musculus gluteus medius; musculus soleus
Equipment and environment: A safe, level walking route
Starting position and set-up: Stand comfortably before beginning to walk.
Step-by-step movement: Walk slowly through the comfortable range.
Range and direction: Use a natural stride and relaxed arm swing.
Breathing: Breathe normally throughout.
Beginner dose and rest: Walk for five minutes with rest as needed.
Expected sensation: Mild effort without sharp symptoms.
Regression: Walk for less time.
Progression: Add time gradually.
Common errors and corrections: Stiffening the shoulders—Relax the arms.
Evidence category: Activity and self-management
Evidence strength: Practical exercise description
Source: Catalogue technique notes
